title: apcore ACL Configuration Schema
description: JSON Schema for validating ACL YAML configuration files. Based on PROTOCOL_SPEC Section 6.

version.description: ACL configuration version. MAJOR.MINOR or MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. The PATCH component is optional because every documented ACL example in this repository uses the two-part form `"1.0"` (docs/features/acl-system.md, docs/guides/acl-configuration.md, examples/acl/agent-tool-governance.yaml) — a full-semver pattern rejected the repository's own shipped example. No SDK reads this field.

default_effect.description: Default effect when no rule matches a caller/target pair. MUST be 'allow' or 'deny'. Defaults to 'deny' for security.

rules.description: Ordered list of ACL rules. Rules are evaluated in DEFINITION ORDER using a first-match-wins strategy — the first rule whose caller and target patterns both match determines the decision (PROTOCOL_SPEC §6.3). They are NOT sorted by priority, and there is no deny-over-allow precedence at equal priority.

ACLRule.description: A single ACL rule. The property set is CLOSED (`additionalProperties: false`) and PROTOCOL_SPEC §6.1 requires an unrecognised key to be rejected at load with `ACLRuleError`: a key nothing evaluates is silently dropped otherwise, which widens an `allow` rule with no warning. `id`, `actions` and `priority` were reserved here for future versions and are evaluated by no implementation; they are removed from this list rather than left declared, because a declared property is exactly what `additionalProperties: false` cannot catch — which is how `actions: ["describe"]` came to grant `execute` (#107).

callers.description: List of caller module ID patterns. Supports wildcards: '*' matches any characters. Special values: '@external' for top-level/external calls, '@system' for internal system calls.

targets.description: List of target module ID patterns. Supports wildcards: '*' matches any characters.

effect.description: The effect to apply when this rule matches. 'allow' permits the call, 'deny' rejects it.

approval.description: Whether a call matching this rule must be put to a human before it runs (PROTOCOL_SPEC §6.1.6). Orthogonal to `effect`: authorization and approval requirement are two independent results, and folding them into one enumeration would make "denied and needs approval" representable. Absent means `not_required`, so every rule written before v1.28.0 keeps its meaning. `required` on a `deny` rule MUST be rejected at load — the combination means nothing, and acting on half of a governance rule is the failure §6.1.5 exists to end.

description.description: Human-readable description of the rule's purpose.

RuleConditions.description: Additional conditions for rule matching (beyond caller/target patterns). All keys are AND-ed. The properties below are the conditions every SDK provides; the set is OPEN because `register_condition()` (PROTOCOL_SPEC §6.1) lets a deployment add its own condition keys at runtime, so a key not listed here is valid exactly when a handler has been registered for it. An unregistered key is not a schema error — it is an unevaluable condition at check time, which denies on a `deny` rule and never grants on an `allow` rule (PROTOCOL_SPEC §6.1.1). `time_window` was listed here as though it were built in; no SDK registers such a handler and docs/guides/acl-configuration.md presents it as a custom-handler example, so it is now validated as any other custom key.

identity_types.description: Only match when the caller's identity type is one of these values.

items.description: An identity type. PROTOCOL_SPEC §5 declares this a free-form string; the well-known values are shown in examples. conformance/fixtures/acl_agent_scoping.json uses `ai`, which a closed enum rejected.

roles.description: Only match when the caller has at least one of these roles. Named `roles` per PROTOCOL_SPEC §6.3; the schema previously called this `identity_roles`, a name that appears in no document, example or fixture.

max_call_depth.description: Only match when call chain depth does not exceed this value.

$or.description: Compound: passes if ANY sub-condition object passes; each sub-object's keys are AND-ed internally. Sub-objects MAY nest further compound operators. PROTOCOL_SPEC §6.3.

$not.description: Compound: passes if the wrapped condition object FAILS. An empty object MUST evaluate to false (fail-closed). PROTOCOL_SPEC §6.3.

arguments.description: Structure-only predicates over the call's argument KEYS (PROTOCOL_SPEC §6.1.7). No predicate reads a value: redaction is driven by the module's input schema, so a module without one gets none, and the ACL runs at Step 4 while input validation runs at Step 7 — key presence is the only question well-defined on what is available. Reads the governance projection of §6.1.8, never the raw arguments and never `redacted_inputs`.

has_key.description: Passes when ANY named key is present in the call's arguments.

has_all_keys.description: Passes when EVERY named key is present.

has_none_of.description: Passes when NONE of the named keys is present.

enabled.description: Whether to enable ACL audit logging.

include_denied.description: Whether to log denied access attempts.
